prompt_latex: Classify the discontinuity of f(x) = \dfrac{x^{2} - 1}{x - 1} at x = 1 and say how to remove it.

prompt_parts.text: Classify the discontinuity of f(x) =
at x = 1 and say how to remove it.

worked_solution: f(1) is undefined (0/0), so f is not continuous at 1
(x − 1)(x + 1)/(x − 1) = x + 1 for x ≠ 1, so the limit as x → 1 is 2
The limit exists, so it is a removable discontinuity (a hole at (1, 2))
final_answer: removable discontinuity at x = 1; defining f(1) = 2 fixes it

source: BC Calculus 12 content: methods of integration (substitution, integration by parts); original
prompt_latex: Evaluate \int  from 0 to 1 of x e^{x^{2}} dx.
prompt_plain: Evaluate ∫ from 0 to 1 of x e^(x²) dx.

prompt_parts.text: Evaluate ∫ from 0 to 1 of x e^(x²) dx.

worked_solution: Let u = x², du = 2x dx, so x dx = du/2
Change limits: x = 0 gives u = 0; x = 1 gives u = 1
(1/2) ∫ from 0 to 1 of e^u du = (1/2)[e^u] from 0 to 1

source: BC Calculus 12 content: methods of integration (substitution, integration by parts); original
prompt_latex: Use integration by parts to find \int  x \cos x dx.
prompt_plain: Use integration by parts to find ∫ x cos x dx.

prompt_parts.text: Use integration by parts to find ∫ x cos x dx.

worked_solution: u = x, dv = cos x dx, so du = dx, v = sin x
∫ x cos x dx = x sin x − ∫ sin x dx
= x sin x + cos x + C
final_answer: x sin x + cos x + C

prompt_latex: Evaluate \int  from 1 to e of x \ln x dx.
prompt_plain: Evaluate ∫ from 1 to e of x ln x dx.

prompt_parts.text: Evaluate ∫ from 1 to e of x ln x dx.

worked_solution: Parts: u = ln x, dv = x dx, so du = dx/x, v = x²/2
= [(x²/2) ln x] from 1 to e − ∫ from 1 to e of (x/2) dx

prompt_latex: Find the area enclosed by y = x^{2} and y = 2x.
prompt_plain: Find the area enclosed by y = x² and y = 2x.

prompt_parts.text: Find the area enclosed by y = x² and y = 2x.

worked_solution: Intersections: x² = 2x gives x = 0 and x = 2
Area = ∫ from 0 to 2 of (2x − x²) dx = [x² − x³/3] from 0 to 2
